correctness.rationale: The identity dE/dt = lambda*x² - b*|x|*(|x|-1)_+ holds for every solution. Two near-grazing arcs each have width 2 sqrt(2 delta) and total dissipation coefficient 8 sqrt(2)/3. The harmonic comparison and a perturbation estimate uniform in delta=s lambda^(2/3) give the return displacement lambda[pi-(8 sqrt(2)/3)b s^(3/2)+o(1)]. Its monotone reduced root fixes C_b. Liouville and the crossing-speed ratio yield the transverse multiplier; the outside-core time is 4 sqrt(2 delta)+o(sqrt delta). Small-parameter signs and strict return-map contraction on the scaling annulus establish existence, local uniqueness and attraction. Exact symbolic integration and finite-parameter Poincare diagnostics were rerun from the package checker. The proof does not infer the asymptotic from finite experiments.

value.rationale: The boundary of the harmonic period annulus is the natural finite-amplitude grazing threshold for the minimal symmetric three-zone piecewise-linear oscillator. The noninteger 2/3 amplitude onset and distinct 1/3 transverse relaxation exponent, including their exact coefficients and a uniform Poincare normal form, quantify the orbit-selection/stability tradeoff that limit-cycle count theorems do not provide. This is a motivated bifurcation asymptotic, not a renamed finite-parameter numerical case.
